definitions.explanation: The tendency to become angry or frustrated quickly. As an adjective, describes a person who is easily irritated.

examples.japanese: {短気|たんき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{損気|そんき}。
examples.english: A short temper leads to loss. (Proverb: Haste makes waste.)
My father is short-tempered and gets angry right away.

examples.japanese: {短気|たんき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{起|お}こさないで→起こす：01234_okosu⟧、⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦{待|ま}って→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Don't lose your temper — please wait a little longer.

notes:
FORMS:
- Predicative: {短気|たんき}だ
- Modifier: {短気|たんき}な + noun
- As noun: {短気|たんき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{起|お}こす→起こす：01234_okosu⟧ (to lose one's temper)

PROVERB:
{短気|たんき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{損気|そんき} is a well-known saying meaning that impatience leads to disadvantage. {損気|そんき} is a made-up word created to rhyme with {短気|たんき}.

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{気|き}が{短|みじか}い→気が短い：06882_kigamijikai⟧ has the same meaning but is a phrase rather than a single word. ⟦{怒|おこ}りっぽい→怒りっぽい：30581_okorippoi⟧ means "easily angered" and focuses more on the emotional reaction.
